This is the one pass criterion a machine cannot supply: whether a maintainer
would actually take the patch. The notes below record the evidence gathered
while capturing the baseline; the `disposition` values are marked NEEDS-REVIEW
because they are an assessment, not the maintainer's judgement.

evidence: The gap is a false positive: paymentMethodOrder already exists in mobile at the base commit
src/types/AllApiDataTypes/ClientResponseType.res:346  paymentMethodOrder: array<string>
src/routes/NavigationRouter.res:114                   nativeProp.configuration.paymentMethodOrder
src/headless/HeadlessCommon.res:767                   nativeProp.configuration.paymentMethodOrder
The seed gap's rationale ('no merchant-configurable ordering option') is factually wrong.
Having found the feature present, the agent instead changed existing sort behaviour:
card-alias matching, inverted -1 semantics, and last-match-wins in sortCustomerPaymentMethods.
Build passed and the verifier returned {pass:true, issues:[]}, so every gate approved it.
Deterministic validators flag size/single_file only — they cannot see that the gap was unreal.
Analyst timed out at 600s in the 'analysing' phase; no diff, no patch row.
Tool calls: Grep 12, Read 10, Bash 15 — for an agent configured read-only.
Root cause was the --allowed-tools finding: the tier was never enforced, so the
analyst shelled out instead of reading and exhausted its budget.
Re-run after the denylist fix before treating this as a model-quality signal.
23.9 min, build GREEN, 46 Edit + 3 Write calls — a substantial implementation.
The verifier produced three specific, file:line-accurate defects:
1. isInstallmentValid not gated on payment method; showInstallments lives in app-level
context and is never reset on tab change -> dead Pay button with an unreachable error.
2. The same ungated flags feed FormStatusEmitter, so a stale card checkbox makes the SDK
emit hasRequiredFields=true for unrelated non-card methods.
3. InstallmentOptions keeps selectedIndex locally while the plan lives in context, so on
remount the list reopens with no radio selected.
The pipeline then DELETED the branch and discarded everything, telling the user to regenerate.
This is the clearest possible case for the bounded repair loop: three actionable findings
against a green-building implementation that was close to correct.
